newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope worried by Albania crisis, urges dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Pope worried by Albania crisis, urges dialogue.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Sunday he was worried by "dramatic moments of violence" in Albania and called for dialogue to overcome what he called intransigent and egotistical positions.

"Only with the respect of all and with a constructive dialogue can dignified solutions be found for everyone," he told pilgrims in St Peter's Square in his weekly Angelus address, in which he also referred to events in Zaire, Jerusalem and Lima.
The Polish Pontiff highlighted the murder of nuns and priests in Zaire, Israel's new settlement plans which he said could badly damage the peace process, and the hostage crisis in Peru.
"These are painful situations which are born of intransigent and egotistical positions," he said.

Talks between Albanian President Sali Berisha and opposition parties on ending an armed rebellion in the south remained deadlocked after eight hours of talks on Saturday but were likely to resume on Sunday.

The West has stepped up mediation efforts as rebels maintained their hold on the south. At least 20 people have been killed in the revolt, sparked off by the collapse of shady investment schemes in January which swallowed the savings of thousands in Europe's poorest country.
